title: Canada Raises Study Permit Financial Requirement to CAD 23,448 Starting September 1
excerpt: International students applying for Canadian study permits must now show higher proof of living expenses, with the new threshold effective for applications filed from September 1, 2026.
body:
• Canada's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has raised the minimum living expense requirement for study permit applicants to CAD 23,448 for a single student, up from CAD 22,895 — an increase of CAD 553.
  • The new requirement takes effect for applications submitted on or after September 1, 2026, and applies to all provinces and territories except Quebec.
  • Students with accompanying family members face even steeper requirements, with a family of three needing CAD 35,888 and a family of seven requiring CAD 62,054.
  • The living expense figure is separate from tuition and transportation costs, pushing the total realistic financial threshold past CAD 40,000 for most applicants.

International students planning to study in Canada will need to demonstrate access to more money when applying for study permits starting Monday. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) updated its proof of financial support page on August 28, confirming that applications submitted on or after September 1, 2026 must show CAD 23,448 in living expenses for a single applicant studying outside Quebec.

The previous threshold of CAD 22,895 — which applied to applications filed between January 1, 2025 and August 31, 2026 — has been replaced with the updated figure, representing a 2.4 percent increase, according to CIC News.

What the Numbers Look Like

The annual adjustment, based on 75 percent of Statistics Canada's Low-Income Cut-Off (LICO), affects applicants across all family sizes. According to IRCC's updated table, the living expense requirements for applications filed from September 1 are:

A single applicant must show CAD 23,448. A student with one family member needs CAD 29,192. A family of three requires CAD 35,888, while a family of four must demonstrate CAD 43,572. Larger families face progressively higher thresholds, with each additional family member beyond seven adding CAD 6,318 to the requirement.

These amounts cover living expenses only. First-year tuition fees and round-trip transportation to and from Canada must be demonstrated separately, pushing the total financial burden well above CAD 40,000 for most program enrollees.

Broader Financial Scrutiny

The increase comes alongside tighter scrutiny of financial documentation. IRCC updated its officer instructions in July 2026, requiring immigration officers to assess the source of an applicant's funds in all cases — not just in what were previously deemed "high-risk" circumstances, according to CIC News.

"Officers look at both amount and source. A large unexplained deposit just before filing is a common problem. Settled, traceable funds are stronger than a last-minute transfer."

— JSR Immigration & Legals

Applicants must provide bank statements covering the past six months, including the month of filing or the month before, along with documentation explaining the source of any funds. Acceptable proof includes student loans, scholarship letters, Guaranteed Investment Certificates (GICs), paid tuition receipts, and letters from financial supporters with proof of their occupation and relationship to the applicant.

Impact on Indian Students

The change is particularly significant for Indian students, who have consistently been among the largest groups of international students in Canada. India was the top source country for Canadian study permits before Ottawa imposed a cap on new permits in 2024 amid concerns about housing and immigration system strain.

The requirement increase, while modest in percentage terms, adds to a financial bar that has risen sharply in recent years. Just two years ago, the living expense threshold stood at CAD 10,000. In January 2024, it was more than doubled to CAD 20,635 to reflect surging housing and living costs in Canadian cities.

For students applying with family members, the increase is larger in absolute terms — a family of seven now needs CAD 1,465 more than under the previous requirement.

Quebec Has Separate, Higher Rules

Students headed to Quebec face a different set of financial requirements administered by the province's immigration ministry. A single Quebec-bound applicant must show CAD 24,617, nearly CAD 1,200 more than the rest-of-Canada figure, under rules that took effect January 1, 2026.

What Applicants Should Do Now

Immigration consultants are advising students to verify the applicable table based on their filing date, not their program start date. Applications filed on or before August 31, 2026 are still assessed under the previous amounts. Students planning to submit after September 1 should budget the new figures and ensure their funds are settled and traceable well in advance of filing.

The update does not change Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) requirements, the study permit cap, or work-hour limits. It only affects the living expense component of the financial assessment.
